local_calendar.t: On November 3, 2026, without party labels, Hawaii County elects the council members for districts 4, 5 and 6, Honolulu County (the City and County of Honolulu) the council members for districts IV and VI, Kauai County its mayor and all seven council members, and Maui County its mayor and all nine council members. The other council seats up this year (Hawaii County districts 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9 and Honolulu County districts II and VIII) were decided at the August 8 primary, where the Office of Elections' list marks one candidate for each Elected After Primary, so they are not on the November ballot. In 2028, by the Office of Elections' Contest Schedule, Hawaii County elects its mayor and its prosecuting attorney, Honolulu County its mayor, its prosecuting attorney and the council members for districts I, III, V, VII and IX, and Kauai County its prosecuting attorney; the schedule lists no city, township, school board or special district office, and Kalawao County, which state law puts under the Department of Health, elects no county officers.

local_coverage.t: Loaded from the Office of Elections' 2026 Candidate Report, read on September 30, 2026: the 17 county contests on the November 3 ballot (2 for mayor and 15 for 21 council seats) and the 44 candidates the report marks In General, in 4 of Hawaii's 5 counties. Not on the November ballot and not shown: the eight seats decided at the August 8 primary, 49 candidates who lost in that primary, 22 people who took out nomination papers and never filed them and 1 who withdrew. For Honolulu County council district IV the report's marks and the certified August 8 count do not line up; the contest is shown as the report marks it and is named among the gaps. Not loaded: county charter amendments and other ballot questions, which a candidate list does not carry, and the August 8 primary's fields and votes for county offices. The report gives no ballot positions (state law has the names for an office printed in alphabetical order) and names no write-in candidates.
local_coverage.s: State of Hawaii Office of Elections, 2026 Candidate Report (county offices); Hawaii Revised Statutes section 11-115 (the order of names on the ballot)

gaps.w: why the one who placed second on August 8 is not on the November list
gaps.r: The Office of Elections' Candidate Report marks In General the candidates who placed first and third in the certified August 8 count for this seat and marks the candidate who placed second In Primary, without saying why; the contest is shown here as the report marks it.
